name: Indian Pudding Without Eggs
description: Historical recipe from Miss Leslie's Complete Cookery (1851). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: a quart or more of Indian meal
ingredients.originalText: a quart or more of Indian meal
ingredients.quantityText: a quart or more of Indian meal

ingredients.name: grated peel and juice of a large lemon or orange
ingredients.originalText: grated peel and juice of a large lemon or orange

instructions.text: Boil some cinnamon in a quart of milk, and then strain it
While the milk is hot, stir into it a pint of molasses
Add by degrees a quart or more of Indian meal so as to make a thick batter
Improve it by the grated peel and juice of a large lemon or orange
Tie it very securely in a thick cloth, leaving room for it to swell, and pasting up the tying-place with a lump of flour and water
Put it into a pot of boiling water, having ready a kettle to fill it up as it boils away
Hang it over a good fire, and keep it boiling hard for four or five hours
Eat it warm with molasses and butter

source.author: Eliza Leslie
source.originalInstructions:
1. Boil some cinnamon in a quart of milk, and then strain it
2. While the milk is hot, stir into it a pint of molasses
3. Add by degrees a quart or more of Indian meal so as to make a thick batter
4. Improve it by the grated peel and juice of a large lemon or orange
5. Tie it very securely in a thick cloth, leaving room for it to swell, and pasting up the tying-place with a lump of flour and water
6. Put it into a pot of boiling water, having ready a kettle to fill it up as it boils away
7. Hang it over a good fire, and keep it boiling hard for four or five hours
8. Eat it warm with molasses and butter
